summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, a mechanical aortic valve, and extensive cardiovascular disease was admitted for substernal chest pain during dialysis. She had elevated troponins without EKG changes, consistent with NSTEMI, and was managed initially with nitroglycerin and blood pressure control. Due to recent gastrointestinal bleeding and elevated INR, cardiac catheterization was delayed until anticoagulation was stabilized. A drug-eluting stent was placed in the mid-LAD artery on hospital day 5, after which her chest pain resolved. She was treated for volume overload with three dialysis sessions, improving pulmonary congestion. A possible pneumonia was ruled out, and antibiotics were discontinued. Her INR was maintained at a new target of 1.8–2.5 to balance clotting and bleeding risks. She was discharged home with home health services on dual anticoagulation (warfarin and clopidogrel), with aspirin to be discontinued after one month, and instructions to continue dialysis, wound care for a left heel ulcer, and outpatient follow-up.
